title: Round-trip core of the Razborov encoding
statement: Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$ and in which no term repeats a variable (within a single term, any two literals on the same variable are equal). Given a fuel budget, a partial decision path, and restrictions $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, let the encoding procedure, started with empty auxiliary data, return a restriction $\rho^\ast$ together with an output list $c$; let $D$ denote the decoding procedure run on $c$ with a fuel budget $m$ and starting restrictions $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$. Suppose that $\sigma$ is free wherever $\rho_0$ is free; that on every variable left free by $\rho_0$ both $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$ agree with $\rho^\ast$; that on every variable fixed by $\rho_0$ one has $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}} = \sigma$ and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}} = \rho_0$; and that $m$ is at least one more than the length of $c$. Then the restriction returned by $D$ equals $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: width of f is at most w
sigma is free wherever rho_0 is free (hE)
sigma_dec agrees with the encoder output on rho_0-free variables (hA)
rho_0_dec agrees with the encoder output on rho_0-free variables (hB)
sigma_dec equals sigma on rho_0-fixed variables (hC)
rho_0_dec equals rho_0 on rho_0-fixed variables (hD)
decoder fuel is at least length of encoder output plus one (hfuel)
caveat: The statement is phrased in terms of the internal fuel-parametrized recursive workers `razborovEncode.go` and `razborovDecode.go`, which are not among the supplied definitions and have no standard mathematical name; the encoding and decoding procedures, their fuel budgets, path prefix, auxiliary accumulator, and paired outputs are implementation scaffolding of a formalized proof, so this is a generalized inductive invariant rather than a self-standing mathematical theorem. The prose describes these helpers abstractly, but faithful informalization is inherently limited.
replaced:
The generalized round-trip statement: for a DNF $f$ of width at most $w$ with distinct
variables per term, given decoder states $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$
that satisfy the round-trip invariants relative to the encoder output and enough decoder
fuel, the first component of the decoder run on the encoder's output list equals the
original $\sigma$. This is the inductive core from which the closed round trip follows.
